title: Embedding horizon model onboarding gates and staggered retirement plan
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary: Plan and implement a gated onboarding and staggered retirement flow for the new 'horizon' embedding model across the embeddings and reranking endpoints. Goal is to allow safe traffic adoption while preserving latency SLOs, embedding contract compatibility, and tenant-level opt-in/out for deprecations.

Background: We need to add 'horizon-v1' (dense 1536-d float16, quant-friendly) to the catalog. The model improves accuracy for semantic search and reranking by ~5-8% on internal benchmarks but has slightly different distribution and slower tail latency under small-batch CPU fallback. Existing lifecycle tickets focus on generic onboarding; this ticket defines an automated, observable gate-and-retire flow that minimizes customer disruption and supports per-tenant pinning and aliases.

Objectives and success criteria:
- Safe rollout path from shadow -> canary -> ramp -> tenant opt-in -> default swap -> soft retirement.
- Maintain embedding endpoint p95 <= existing p95 + 10ms during canary and ramp phases; p99 must remain within SLA bounds.
- No semantic-drift regressions exceeding 3% on a set of +10 curated benchmarks and customer prompt sets.
- Rollback and alias fallback must be possible within 15 minutes with zero data loss.
- Telemetry dashboards for per-model latency, cosine distribution shifts, and downstream rerank recall/precision by cohort.

Design decisions and tradeoffs:
- Use model aliasing instead of replacing model IDs: consumers continue to call "embed-text:latest" while rollout maps alias -> concrete variant. This reduces required client changes but requires server-side alias mapping logic and expanded compatibility checks.
- Implement a two-stage compatibility shim that validates vector dimension and dtype at activation time and rejects activations that would change contract shape without migration support.
- Prefer JVM-side batching runtime kernels for horizon-v1 on GPU; configure CPU fallback only for burst scenarios to avoid decoding p99 spikes. This accepts a small complexity increase in the routing layer to prefer GPU hosts with horizon-optimized kernels.
- Shadow runs must be computed asynchronously and a small percentage (<2%) of traffic instrumented synchronously for fairness metrics.

Rollout plan (detailed):
1) Shadowing (Week 0): route 100% traffic to primary model; compute horizon-v1 vectors in shadow asynchronously for telemetry. No serving change.
2) Canary cohort (Week 1): select 3 low-risk tenant cohorts (internal, opt-in beta customers). Sync compute for 5% of their calls. Monitor latency p95/p99, cosine similarity distributions, and rerank recall. Gate: p99 latency increase <= 20ms and rerank recall delta <= 2%.
3) Controlled ramp (Week 2-3): expand canary cohorts to 20 tenants and gradually increase traffic percentage by 10% per day if gates pass. Add auto-rollover: if latency or quality regressions are detected, rollback to previous alias.
4) Tenant opt-in window (Week 4): surface console toggle and API flag to opt-in tenants to horizon-v1. Encourage users via in-console A/B test runner and per-tenant benchmarks.
5) Default swap & soft retirement (Week 5-8): if metrics remain healthy, change alias mapping to route default traffic to horizon-v1 while keeping previous model as a fallback variant for 30 days. Start issuing deprecation notices in console and billing emails with managed pin/unpin options.
6) Final retirement (Week 9+): allow tenants to migrate; remove the retired model after 90 days of low traffic and zero opt-ins.

Telemetry & gating signals to implement:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-model, per-route, per-tenant. Alert if p99 increases by >15ms for >10m.
- Quality: cosine similarity shift histograms, recall@k for reranking benchmark sets, human-eval regression checks.
- Cost: token and compute cost delta by tenant; if >12% increase for a major tenant, mark high cost-impact.
- Usage: cohort breakdown (internal/beta/public), opt-in/opt-out counts.

Compatibility and API contract work:
- Add a model metadata field `embedding_schema` returned by model catalog API describing dtype, dimension, and quantization flags. The embeddings gateway must validate client request compatibility when switching alias mapping.
- If dimension changes (unlikely), provide an adapter path in the console to auto-resize stored vectors (best-effort) and mark affected dashboards.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Immediate rollback: alias switch back and traffic re-route; warm KV caches by replaying recent prefixes for top 50 tenants. Target fallback time <15m.
- Gradual rollback: pause ramp and revert only canary cohorts.
- Incident playbook reference: link to confluence incident postmortem template.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- How to handle cross-tenant vector indexes when some tenants upgrade and others don't? (coord with retrieval infra team).
- Policy for auto-requantization of tenant indexes if horizon uses different quant profile.
- Should we include a cost-offset program for enterprise customers who opt into early horizon adoption?

Deliverables (engineering scope):
- Alias mapping implementation in model catalog (server + console UI).
- Gating service that evaluates telemetry windows and emits pass/fail decisions.
- Telemetry dashboards: latency/quality/cost per cohort.
- Migration APIs for tenant pinning and vector resize helpers.
- Documentation: console opt-in flow, API flag docs, deprecation messages.
